about: The 2 x AA design that follows from the owner's rulings of 22 Nov 2026 (two AA cells, a physical off switch, the Adafruit MPU-6050 breakout, the detection rules, the Arduino sketch, the prototype costs added up). Every row comes from docs/design/baggage-claims-device.md and names its section. Parts and wires of the 3 x AA design that the rulings supersede are changed or retired only while they still read as seeded; a row a person has changed is left alone. Every figure that is an estimate says so in its text.

rows.setBody: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3 (ESP32-S3, 8 MB flash), 21 x 17.5 mm, fed 3.3 V at its 3V3 pin from the boost regulator; radios never started. Replaces the Rev A board (a Waveshare ESP32-S3 Mini on a 4.5-4.9 V bus, which two AA cells cannot supply). Price: an estimate from the maker's list price as recalled, not read on 22 Nov.

Adafruit MPU-6050 6-DoF accelerometer and gyro breakout (product 3886): I2C address 0x68, 3 to 5 V in, own regulator, level shifting and 10 k pull-ups, 26.0 x 17.8 x 4.6 mm, four 2.5 mm mounting holes. The owner's ruling of 22 Nov: this breakout is the base (Rev A: a GY-521 board). Prices read on the maker's page on 22 Nov: 12.95 for 1 to 9, 10.36 for 100 or more.

geometry.basisSource: Outline from the maker's product page (26.0 x 17.8 x 4.6 mm)

rows.setBody: I2S class-D amplifier breakout, MAX98357A, mono, 2.7 to 5.5 V; it drives the speaker directly and is shut down by its SD pin. Replaces the DFPlayer Mini, which needs 3.2 to 5 V, idles at about 20 mA and takes its clips from a microSD card; the clips now live in the controller's flash. Price: an estimate from the maker's list price as recalled.

40 mm 4 ohm 3 W paper-cone speaker with leads, about 20 mm deep. 4 ohm, not 8: on a 3.3 V rail a 4 ohm speaker takes about 1.0 W where an 8 ohm one takes about 0.6 W (calculated). Sensitivity of this class: 80.5 dB at 1 W and 1 m (one maker's data sheet, read 22 Nov). Price: an estimate.

geometry.basisSource: 40 mm diameter, 20 mm high: a reseller's page for a 40 mm 4 ohm speaker, read 22 Nov

rows.setBody: 2 x AA holder with leads, cells in series. The owner's ruling of 22 Nov: two AA alkaline cells (Rev A: three). Price: an estimate.

setData.search: 2 AA battery holder with wire leads

rows.setBody: AA alkaline, two cells (no lithium). About 3.2 V new and 2.0 V at the end of their useful life (1.0 V a cell). Price: the documents' $2.50 for three cells, taken per cell.

Slide switch, SPST or SPDT used as SPST, rated at least 1 A at 6 V DC, in the battery's positive lead: off is a true disconnect, nothing is powered. The rating matters: the regulator draws up to about 0.8 A from nearly flat cells during a loud clip (calculated).

Solderable perfboard cut to a 70 x 22 mm strip: the carrier for the controller, the motion sensor and the amplifier, with the regulator, MOSFET and capacitors beside it. (Rev A: the whole 5 x 7 cm board.)

rows.why: the 1 k series resistor belonged to the DFPlayer's serial line; the 2 x AA design has no DFPlayer
the microSD card belonged to the DFPlayer; in the 2 x AA design the clips are in the controller's flash

rows.title: Boost regulator
rows.body: 3.3 V step-up regulator module, 0.5 to 5.5 V in, of the class of the Pololu U1V11F3 (12 x 15 x 3 mm): makes the regulated 3.3 V rail from two AA cells and keeps it there as they run down. Switch current limit typically 1.2 to 1.5 A (maker's page). Its no-load current sets the sleep current and must be measured: the maker says under 1 mA. Price: an estimate.

geometry.basisSource: 12 x 15 x 3 mm: the maker's product page

rows.title: Reverse-battery MOSFET
rows.body: P-channel MOSFET, logic level (fully on at 1.8 V gate drive, about 0.1 ohm), SOT-23 on a small adapter board, in the battery's positive lead after the switch: cells put in backwards cannot reach the regulator. Price: an estimate.

rows.title: Bulk capacitor
rows.body: 470 uF 6.3 V (or 10 V) low-ESR electrolytic on the 3.3 V rail at the amplifier: it carries the peaks of a clip so the rail does not dip and reset the controller. Price: an estimate.

rows.title: Battery sense capacitor
rows.body: 100 nF ceramic from the battery-sense midpoint to ground: the two 1 M resistors are too high a source for the controller's converter without it. Price: an estimate.

rows.title: Battery sense resistor, upper
rows.body: 1 M ohm 1/4 W from the battery side of the regulator to the sense midpoint. With the lower one it halves the battery voltage for the controller and draws 1.5 uA. Price: the documents' figure for a resistor.

rows.title: Battery sense resistor, lower
rows.body: 1 M ohm 1/4 W from the sense midpoint to ground.

rows.title: Amplifier shutdown pull-down
rows.body: 10 k ohm 1/4 W from the amplifier's SD pin to ground: the amplifier stays shut down whenever the controller is asleep or resetting (its board pulls SD up through 1 M).

rows.why: the switch now feeds the reverse-battery MOSFET and the regulator; there is no 4.5 V VIN bus
the DFPlayer and its serial line are not in the 2 x AA design

rows.setBody: 3.3 V from the rail to the breakout's VIN (it accepts 3 to 5 V); its own regulator then drops a little, which the sensor tolerates (2.375 V minimum, data sheet as recalled). Never connect GND to VIN.

rows.appendBody: D5 is GPIO6 on the XIAO ESP32S3.

rows.setBody: 10 k pull-ups are on the Adafruit breakout, so none are added. Digital 3.3 V. D4 is GPIO5 on the XIAO ESP32S3.
Active low and latched until the firmware reads the sensor's status. D1 (GPIO2) wakes the controller from deep sleep.
3.3 V straight from the regulator's output, on its own wire, so the amplifier's current does not pass through the controller's pads.
Either polarity. Bridged class-D drive from the amplifier's + and - terminals into 4 ohm, about 1 W at most on the 3.3 V rail; neither lead may touch ground. Keep the leads short and twisted.

rows.appendBody: D3 is GPIO4; it also wakes the controller from deep sleep.

rows.body: Meter the rail before fitting the controller: 3.17 to 3.43 V (3.3 V, 4 %). Never plug in USB while the switch is on.

rows.appendBody: Ruling of 22 Nov: as in the documents. The documents' 8 to 14 g window cannot be measured on a +/-8 g range, so the range is +/-16 g and the filter 94 Hz; the threshold starts at 6 g and is tuned with the logging mode. A bump that ends a flight is that flight's landing, not a second gag.

setData.trigger: Peak of 6 g or more on the +/-16 g range, not within 1.5 s of a flight; 1 s before the next

rows.appendBody: Kept as the documents have it, with one addition: the stillness must follow a lift within 3 s, so a bag that is simply left alone does not qualify. Reported when the stillness ends.

setData.trigger: A lift (0.25 g or more), then dead still for 3.5 to 6 s, then moved

rows.appendBody: Ruling of 22 Nov: tilt and quick motion, then sustained tilt plus steady carry accelerations. Quick motion is 0.3 g or 60 degrees a second. Carry is 1 s windows with 0.04 to 0.6 g of bounce in three of every four. The gag comes about 4.5 s after the grab (Rev A: 10 s).

setData.trigger: From rest: 20 degrees of tilt and quick motion within 1.5 s, then 4 s of carry at 12 degrees of tilt or more

rows.appendBody: Ruling of 22 Nov: duration over 0.3 s (a fall of 0.44 m). The limit is 0.35 g plus up to 0.45 g for a tumbling bag, because the tag sits up to 0.45 m off the spin axis and then never reads zero. Reported in the air, 0.3 s in; the bump that follows is its landing.

setData.trigger: In the air for 0.3 s with no launch before it: |a| under 0.35 g plus an allowance for spin

rows.appendBody: Ruling of 22 Nov: circular and periodic motion for about 15 s or more, best settings. The turn is measured about the direction of gravity, so the tag's attitude does not matter. A carousel's sideways acceleration is only about 0.02 g, the size of a 1 degree tilt, so it is not used. Turns the other way cancel; turn older than about 40 s fades.

setData.trigger: 15 s of quiet transport with 120 degrees of turn one way about the vertical (4 to 60 degrees a second)

rows.appendBody: The documents' 100 to 400 Hz band cannot exist at a 100 Hz sample rate. The rule is the vibration's size and rhythm in 1 s windows; a cart or a car boot reads the same and is the same gag. A ride that is already turning waits for the carousel decision.

setData.trigger: 8 s of steady vibration, 0.03 to 0.30 g, faster than a walking rhythm, turning under 25 degrees a second

rows.appendBody: On a tag that hangs from a loop this says the tag is upside down, which is not always the bag. Kept, with low confidence, until it is tried on a case.

setData.trigger: The tag's own up axis pointing down (within 25 degrees) for 4 s

rows.appendBody: The controller sleeps and a timer wakes it once, two hours after the motion stopped, to say the line; then it sleeps until moved.

setData.trigger: No motion for 2 hours: one timed wake from deep sleep

rows.title: Detect: Throw
rows.body: The owner's question of 22 Nov: the best way to detect a throw. A throw is a launch, then a flight, then a landing. Launch: in the 0.6 s before the flight, |a| above 1.15 g adding up to 0.08 g-seconds (about 0.8 m/s), or one sample above 2 g. Flight: 0.3 s in the air by the free-fall rule. Landing: 2.5 g or more within 0.3 s of the flight's end. No launch makes it a drop (free-fall); a set-down never gets under the flight limit for 0.3 s; conveyor vibration swings about 1 g and never stays under it.

data.trigger: Launch (0.08 g-seconds above 1.15 g, or 2 g, in the 0.6 s before), then 0.3 s in the air, then a landing of 2.5 g
data.response: A thrown-bag line in the air; the landing does not get its own gag

rows.title: Sensor configuration
rows.body: MPU-6050 at 100 samples a second, 94 Hz filter, +/-16 g and +/-2000 degrees a second, read in batches from its FIFO. Asleep: accelerometer only, 5 wake-ups a second, motion interrupt at about 80 mg (to be confirmed on the bench). The gyro's zero offset (up to 20 degrees a second) is learnt at rest and never from a steady turn.

rows.title: Logging mode for tuning
rows.body: Holding the button while switching on, or sending l over USB, makes the firmware print every sample (time, three accelerations, three rotation rates, tilt, turn, still) and every event at 100 lines a second, and stay awake. Every threshold is a starting value until it has been tuned with recordings from real luggage.

data.trigger: Button held at switch-on, or l over USB

rows.setBody: Two AA alkaline cells in series (the owner's ruling of 22 Nov; Rev A: three), a 3.3 V boost regulator, and a slide switch in the battery lead. Asleep after 45 s without motion; the motion sensor's interrupt or the button wakes it. Sleep current estimated at 0.25 mA at the battery (0.2 to 0.4 mA): above Rev A's 200 uA figure, which Rev A's own parts could not meet either (its audio module idles at about 20 mA).

setData.response: Deep sleep; wake on motion or the button

rows.title: Off switch is a true disconnect
rows.body: The owner's ruling of 22 Nov: a physical OFF switch, in case the airport asks for the device to be disabled; with AA cells it need not be off for flight. The switch is in the battery's positive lead, ahead of everything: off, no part of the circuit is powered and the current is zero.

rows.title: Battery life
rows.body: Estimate, for a stated profile: a travel day is 3 h awake (about 9 mA at the battery), six clips and 21 h asleep (0.25 mA), about 33 mAh; a day at home switched on is about 6 mAh. With 2,000 mAh usable from two AA alkaline cells down to 1.0 V a cell: about 6 months at four travel days a month, about 5 months at eight, about 11 months left switched on and untouched. The documents ask for 3 to 6 months. Every current here is calculated, none measured.

rows.title: Low battery
rows.body: Battery read through a 1 M / 1 M divider with the device awake and silent. Below 2.4 V (1.2 V a cell): clips 3 dB quieter. Below 2.2 V: 6 dB quieter and the low-battery line once. Below 2.0 V, or 1.8 V under a clip's load, or after two brown-out resets: no clips, sleep only. Rev A's threshold (3.3 V for three cells) is the same 1.1 V a cell as the second step.

data.response: Quieter; the low-battery line once; then silent

rows.title: Reverse battery and brown-out
rows.body: Cells fitted backwards must do no harm: a P-channel MOSFET blocks them. A dip of the 3.3 V rail during a clip must not leave the device stuck: the controller's brown-out reset restarts it, the firmware counts such resets and goes quieter after one and silent after two. A 470 uF capacitor at the amplifier carries the peaks.

data.response: No damage; restart, quieter, then silent

rows.title: Drop survival
rows.body: The tag on a suitcase handle must still work after the case is dropped 1.0 m onto concrete, six times, one on each face (an estimate of rough handling; the documents say shocks to 40 g survival). Inside: cells held against their springs by ribs, the speaker and every board fixed, the sensor screwed down. Enclosure walls 2.4 mm PETG or more at the corners.

rows.appendBody: For the 2 x AA design: about 1.0 W into a 4 ohm speaker from the 3.3 V rail, about 80 dB at 1 m with a 40 mm speaker of 80.5 dB at 1 W and 1 m (calculated from a data sheet figure, not measured). That is inside the 85 dBA ceiling and about 5 dB short of the documents' "~85 dBA @1m - loud enough for terminals". Rev A as drawn (an 8 ohm speaker on about 4.7 V) comes to about 1 W as well.
In the Rev B firmware a tap while a clip plays stops the clip; between clips it steps the volume. The button also wakes the device.

rows.setBody: A new sketch was written for the 2 x AA design on 22 Nov 2026: BaggageClaims_MK1_RevB.ino with bc_detect.h and bc_detect.cpp, in Files. Proved on 22 Nov, on a PC: the detection core builds with g++ without a warning and passes 26 host tests on synthetic traces; arduino-cli 1.2.2 with the Arduino-ESP32 4.0.0 core compiles and links the whole sketch for esp32:esp32:XIAO_ESP32S3 with all warnings on and none in the sketch's files (418,264 bytes, 12 % of the 3.3 MB the tool counts; the partitions file gives the application 2 MB). One step was stood in for: Arduino's ctags tool, which adds function prototypes, could not be downloaded here, so a stand-in that adds none was used; the sketch declares its own prototypes, so nothing depends on it. Not proved: a build in the owner's own Arduino IDE with the real ctags, and anything on hardware. Left open for the owner to mark done after his own build. The Rev A sketch in the Drive folder still uses gxDump and gzDump before they are declared.

data.pass: Toss a packed case 1.5 m onto a mat, five times: the log shows THROW then LANDING each time, never FREEFALL or IMPACT, and the thrown-bag line starts before the landing
Let a packed case fall 0.6 m from rest onto a mat, five times: FREEFALL then LANDING each time, never THROW. From 0.2 m: no FREEFALL
On a turntable or a carousel at 5 to 25 degrees a second: CAROUSEL once, between 15 and 25 s after the ride begins. Wheeled in a straight line for 60 s: no CAROUSEL
On a belt or a vibrating cart for 20 s: CONVEYOR once, 8 to 12 s in; none while the case is carried by hand for 60 s
Switch off, meter in series with the battery on its most sensitive range: 0 uA (under the meter's resolution), and 0 V at the regulator input
Awake and being moved, no clip: under 15 mA at the battery, averaged over 10 s (estimate 9 mA)

Loudest clip at full volume, new cells, sound level meter (A-weighted, fast) at 1 m on the grille's axis: record the peak. Pass under 85 dBA; record the shortfall against the documents' 85 (estimate about 80)
On a bench supply in place of the cells: at 2.3 V clips are quieter, at 2.1 V the low-battery line plays once, at 1.9 V no clip plays; no reset loop at any voltage from 3.2 V down to 1.5 V
Cells fitted backwards for one minute, then correctly: no current over 1 mA while reversed, and the device works afterwards
Tag on a packed case, dropped 1.0 m onto concrete, once on each of six faces: the tag stays closed, nothing rattles, and it still passes the Drop and Weigh-in tests

rows.body: Run by an agent on 22 Nov 2026 with a stand-in for Arduino's ctags (scripts/firmware-check.sh board with BC_CTAGS_STUB=1): compiled and linked, 418,264 bytes, no warning in the sketch's files. Left not run until the build is repeated with the real Arduino tools (the IDE or a full arduino-cli install).

data.pass: arduino-cli compile for esp32:esp32:XIAO_ESP32S3 with core 4.0.0 finishes with no error (scripts/firmware-check.sh board), and the binary is under the 2 MB application partition

appendData.pass: For the 2 x AA design: meter in series with the battery, 5 min after the last motion. Estimate 0.25 mA (0.2 to 0.4 mA); the documents' 200 uA is not expected to be met. Over 0.4 mA: find the cause (the regulator's own current, the sensor board's LED if it has one) before going on.
For the 2 x AA design: regulator input 2.0 to 3.2 V with two AA cells in and the switch on, 0 V with it off; the 3.3 V rail reads 3.17 to 3.43 V.
With the Rev B firmware the gag comes about 5 s after the grab.

rows.appendBody: That is the Rev A interface. The 2 x AA design has no player module: the controller reads 16-bit mono WAV clips from its own flash and sends them to the amplifier over I2S (bit clock, word select, data), sets the volume as a gain in firmware, and knows itself when a clip is playing.

In the 2 x AA design a pack is a folder (/p1, /p2, /p3) of WAV files in the controller's flash file system, written over USB separately from the firmware. The 5.9 MB set aside hold about 3 minutes of clips at 16 kHz: the ten starter clips in three packs fit; the documents' 128 clips in each of three packs do not, and a pack can no longer be sold as a card. A card socket would bring that back at the cost of sleep current and four more pins.
On the 2 x AA design the port is the XIAO's USB-C, used with the battery switch off. The Rev B log prints one EVT line per event with the governor's verdict, and the logging mode prints every sample.

The Adafruit breakout has four 2.5 mm holes (the maker's page); screw it down through all four on printed posts, with its long edge square to the tag's long axis. Hole spacing 20.3 x 12.7 mm is typical of this board family and must be checked against the maker's drawing before the posts are printed.
The Rev B firmware keeps these rules; with no player module, busy is the firmware's own playing state, and the latches survive deep sleep.
For the 2 x AA design the parts list has 21 lines; lay it out against the app's parts list, not the CSV.

For the 2 x AA design, in this order: (1) power: holder, switch, MOSFET, regulator; meter the rail at 3.17 to 3.43 V before any module is fitted; (2) controller on the rail (3V3 and GND); (3) motion sensor: VIN, GND, SCL to D5, SDA to D4, INT to D1; (4) amplifier: Vin and GND from the regulator, BCLK to D8, LRC to D9, DIN to D10, SD to D2 with 10 k to ground, the 470 uF capacitor across Vin and GND, speaker to + and -; (5) battery sense: 1 M from the regulator input to D0, 1 M and 100 nF from D0 to ground; (6) button from D3 to ground with its 10 k pull-up. Modules are soldered to the strip, not socketed: the 42 mm depth has no room for sockets.
For the 2 x AA design: the rail reads 3.17 to 3.43 V; the regulator input reads the battery (2.0 to 3.2 V); nothing warm after 30 s.

For the 2 x AA design: battery switch off, USB-C in. Arduino-ESP32 core 4.0.0, board XIAO_ESP32S3, no library to install. Put BaggageClaims_MK1_RevB.ino, bc_detect.h, bc_detect.cpp and the partitions file (renamed partitions.csv) in a folder named BaggageClaims_MK1_RevB, build and upload. Expect "BAGGAGE CLAIMS MK1 Rev B ... MPU OK FS OK" at 115200 baud; "FS FAIL" until the clips are loaded.

For the 2 x AA design: no card. Save each clip as 16-bit mono WAV at 16 kHz, named by class and number (/p1/impact_1.wav, /p1/impact_2.wav, /p1/weigh_1.wav, /p1/grab_1.wav, /p1/freefall_1.wav, /p1/throw_1.wav, /p1/carousel_1.wav, /p1/conveyor_1.wav, /p1/inverted_1.wav, /p1/idle_1.wav, /p1/lowbatt_1.wav), and write the folder to the controller's LittleFS partition over USB.

appendData.pass: For the 2 x AA design the regulator's tolerance is 4 %: 3.17 to 3.43 V.

rows.appendBody: Added up on 22 Nov at the owner's request: the 16 lines of the parts list come to $64.80; the PRD's nine-row table comes to $64.34 under a total line of $64.80; the PRD's cost-table column comes to $58.80. The 2 x AA design's parts come to $72.83 for one unit (estimate), $72.83 a unit for five and $62.69 a unit for a hundred, with the kit lines (wire, perfboard, hardware) left at the documents' figures.
